ch01.card: Part 1 of 10. One question, start to finish.
ch01.s01.c1: Here is a question you can answer in your head. How would a machine do it? This part follows one question through the whole model.
ch01.s01.c2: Four parts: reader, thinker, stop switch and talker. It uses an outside calculator.
ch01.s01.c3: Some parts have a test result. All together, never tested.
ch01.s02.c1: Here is the question. We made it up as an example. Solve it before we do.
ch01.s02.c2: The model works on letters, so every letter gets its own box.
ch01.s03.c1: First, a borrowed reader, trained by someone else, reads the whole question once. Its name is EmbeddingGemma 2.
ch01.s03.c2: Frozen means our practice, which we call training, never changes it.
ch01.s03.c3: Each letter gets 768 numbers from the reader: those of the word piece the letter sits in.
ch01.s03.c4: And the reader has 271,002,624 numbers. We did not set a single one.
ch01.s04.c1: A small window lets each letter see 4 letters on each side.
ch01.s04.c2: This one is ours, learned from scratch in our practice. The reader was borrowed.
ch01.s04.c3: Does it matter? In small tests at the 3 million size, every reader without it failed the letter-code puzzles.
ch01.s05.c1: Now the thinker, the part that loops. One lap around the question is one round.
ch01.s05.c2: In each round it looks at the whole question, passes notes, and thinks. A team of note-takers.
ch01.s05.c3: The same learned settings are used every round. Only its notes change.
ch01.s06.c1: In round 1 the thinker looks at every letter and passes notes.
ch01.s06.c2: Tested version: no call after round 1, so the slot stays empty. A call asks the outside calculator.
ch01.s06.c3: In the version we tested, the first call comes after round 2. Hold on to that slip.
ch01.s07.c1: Tested version: after round 2 the call writer reads its first control vector, a list of numbers.
ch01.s07.c2: Then it picks one of 8 operations for its slip, or writes no call. No call is a choice.
ch01.s07.c3: The 8 are add, sub, mul, div, mod, min, max and cmp.
ch01.s08.c1: Tested version: the thinker writes a call as text. A learned pointer finds each number's last digit.
ch01.s08.c2: The code copies one letter at a time to the left, until the learned stop head says stop.
ch01.s08.c3: Some steps are still hand-written code, like flipping the digits into reading order.
ch01.s09.c1: Why a calculator at all? It is an ordinary program, outside the model.
ch01.s09.c2: A call is a line of text. The reader reads the answer, also as text.
ch01.s09.c3: Switch it off, and questions that need a calculation scored 0.0 points out of 100 on all 6 copies.
ch01.s10.c1: The outside calculator gets sub 12, 5 and sends back 7, as plain text.
ch01.s10.c2: Built so far: the letter window alone reads the reply. New design: the whole reader, Gemma too.
ch01.s10.c3: Gemma and the calculator have never run together.
ch01.s11.c1: Round 3 now also sees sub 12, 5 = 7. Can you guess the next slip?
ch01.s11.c2: Tested version: the call writer writes add 7, 3, copying 7 from the reply and 3 from the question.
ch01.s11.c3: The calculator returns 10. The reader reads it, and it joins the notes.
ch01.s12.c1: Some rounds have nothing to calculate, so they write no call.
ch01.s12.c2: In the version we tested, calls come after rounds 2 to 8 only.
ch01.s12.c3: The newest version can call in any round from 2 to 32. It is built, but not tested.
ch01.s13.c1: After each round a small learned switch asks: is it done yet?
ch01.s13.c2: It must run at least 1 round, and at most 32. The 32 is a safety limit.
ch01.s13.c3: A stop ends each turn. The switch is built, never tested.
ch01.s14.c1: The stand-in copies 10 from the last reply, where the thinker points.
ch01.s14.c2: It adds no thinking of its own, so the answer is just the copied 10.
ch01.s14.c3: Planned talker, about 25 million numbers: reads thoughts, writes calls, no pointer.
ch01.s15.c1: Green. Adding the Gemma reader gained 2.67 points out of 100 on 6,040 questions, in 6 of 6 copies, at 3M.
ch01.s15.c2: Green. The calculator outside matched the old calculator-inside model in 6 copies. One check on no-thinking answers missed, but the project owner cleared it.
ch01.s15.c3: Amber: calls in any round, and the stop switch. Built, never tested.
ch01.s15.c4: Grey: the English talker. A placeholder, not built yet.
ch01.s15.c5: Open question: with the Gemma reader, some answers use zero thinking rounds. Everything together: never tested.
ch01.s16.c1: The reader reads each turn's new text. The thinker thinks in rounds.
ch01.s16.c2: The stop switch ends the turn. The talker writes the answer or a call.
ch01.s16.c3: Next, we open each box. First, the reader: why can't we change it?
